transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Miles Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Amir Kovacs (Redwood Product), Evan Morales (AuroraCloud PM), Leila Hammond (AuroraCloud Solutions Architect), Benji Park (AuroraCloud Marketplace Eng), Sana Iqbal (AuroraCloud Security)

Summary: Short sync to align on marketplace listing steps, technical validation for joint reference architecture (especially Private/VPC options), and GTM assets. Heavy focus on security checklist (KMS/SSO), Terraform examples, and roles for validation window.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Miles): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you all hear me?
00:06 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yep loud and clear Miles, thanks for organizing.
00:10 Speaker 1 (Miles): Cool, so quick agenda: marketplace listing requirements, walk through our proposed reference arch for AuroraCloud customers (private deployment), the security signoff items, and then decide next steps. Priya and Amir from our side will cover the technical bits.
00:25 Speaker 3 (Priya): Hi all, I’ll jump into the reference arch in a bit, but first big picture — Redwood wants to make sure the marketplace listing maps to a validated deployment pattern. For AuroraCloud we think two flavors: hosted listing (managed) and private/VPC deployable reference arch.
00:42 Speaker 4 (Leila): That matches what AuroraCloud PM wants. For marketplace we need the image, pricing tiers, deploy automation, and an architecture doc. Question — do you have terraform examples for the private install?
00:54 Speaker 3 (Priya): We have a starter set, yes. Today we’ll go over which bits we’ll hand you and what we expect AuroraCloud to provide — e.g., a staging account, images for the marketplace UI, and the marketplace API credentials.
01:12 Speaker 5 (Benji): On the marketplace side we also validate SSO and billing integration. Our validation team will need to run a deploy in a staging VPC. What does your private deploy require for networking (NAT, egress rules)?
01:25 Speaker 3 (Priya): Good call — our private pack supports both egress-proxy mode and restricted egress via NAT. The reference arch doc includes recommended security groups, salt for KV cache routing, and a note about KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping. Sorry, mouthful — sometimes our doc uses internal names like KV cache and KVS, apologies if that comes out garbled in the transcript.
01:45 Speaker 6 (Sana): On security, we need to confirm SOC 2 controls mapping and how audit logs are forwarded. Do you support customer-managed KMS (bring your own key) for token encryption?
01:55 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes — BYOK is supported via KMS integration. We can outline key rotation, envelope encryption for model weights cache, and the audit log sink. We’ll include a sample CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Log export stanza in the Terraform.
02:12 Speaker 2 (Evan): Can we cover the marketplace listing metadata? We need the tile copy, images, pricing matrix, and any third-party compliance badges. Also, legal requires a statement on data residency.
02:25 Speaker 1 (Miles): For tile copy and images we typically supply marketing-approved blurbs and a logo. For pricing we can propose usage tiers (hosted per-token and a dedicated capacity commit for reserved), and a private deployment license fee. We’ll send suggested pricing ranges but AuroraCloud can map to your billing model.
02:45 Speaker 4 (Leila): One pain point: we often get confused about fallback behavior between hosted and private. If a customer purchases via marketplace and chooses AuroraCloud-managed deploy, who owns the keys and logs?
02:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): Good question. We recommend clear options in the listing: managed by Redwood (we manage keys and logs) vs customer-managed (AuroraCloud customer supplies KMS). We’ll document the responsibilities.
03:12 Speaker 5 (Benji): For validation we need a concrete checklist. Benji to follow up: can Redwood provide a smoke test script that we can run in the staging account?
03:20 Speaker 1 (Miles): Yes — action: Priya will share a smoke test harness (bash/python) + terraform snippets.
03:28 Speaker 7 (Amir): I want to highlight the reference architecture diagram: main components are control plane (Redwood), data plane (deployment on customer AuroraCloud infra), KV cache, and optional prefix caching for prompt workflows. For the listing we’ll attach a simplified diagram and a deeper reference arch in the docs site.
03:48 Speaker 6 (Sana): On auditability — do you ingest audit logs to an external SIEM? How granular are the logs (per-request token id)?
03:55 Speaker 3 (Priya): We emit request-level logs but can mask tokens. We log metadata: request id, model version, latency, and user-id hash. We’ll include retention recommendations and options for pushing logs to the customer SIEM via syslog or cloud logging exports.
04:10 Speaker 2 (Evan): Timeline-wise, AuroraCloud wants the listing live before Q1 promotions. That means we need validation and legal signoff in December. Is that achievable?
04:20 Speaker 1 (Miles): We think so if both sides commit this week — Redwood will ship docs by 12/07, staging validation 12/10, and final listing artifacts 12/14.
04:30 Speaker 4 (Leila): Sounds tight but doable. Supply chain: legal will need the SLA doc and support contacts.
04:36 Speaker 1 (Miles): We’ll send an SLA template and support matrix.
04:40 Speaker 5 (Benji): Technical nit: does Redwood support GPU assignment per tenant in the dedicated pool or is it per model?
04:49 Speaker 3 (Priya): Dedicated pools are per-customer; you can pin model versions and capacity via reserved capacity. We can include a recommended capacity table (concurrent requests, seq length) in the ref arch. We’ll surface quantization profiles too for cost guidance.
05:05 Speaker 6 (Sana): Regarding compliance, is there an SOC 2 report we can review? Also SSO: we need SAML metadata for the integration test.
05:14 Speaker 1 (Miles): We’ll share SOC 2 Type II and our security whitepaper. For SAML SSO we’ll provide metadata and a guide for IdP configuration — we’ll include a sample SAML config in the repo.
05:25 Speaker 7 (Amir): I’ll call out integration points in the reference arch: 1) provisioning via marketplace API, 2) deployment automation (Terraform + Helm), 3) KMS and audit log integration, 4) monitoring hooks (prometheus/exporter) for observability.
05:45 Speaker 2 (Evan): For the marketplace API, can you outline the flow from purchase to deployment? We need to show that in the listing docs.
05:52 Speaker 3 (Priya): Sure — flow: purchase event -> marketplace notifies AuroraCloud -> AuroraCloud provides provisioning webhook -> Redwood control plane creates tenant record -> if private deploy, Terraform triggers customer infra deploy; if managed, Redwood spins up in our dedicated pool and configures tenant keys. We can diagram that for the listing.
06:15 Speaker 5 (Benji): If we do a private deploy via AuroraCloud, what does the CI validation look like? We’ll need an automated smoke test that checks endpoint, SSO, and basic latency SLA.
06:24 Speaker 3 (Priya): Exactly — smoke test checks API health, token issuance via SAML, run a short generation with fixed prompt and validate latency under threshold and correct model version. We’ll provide the harness.
06:38 Speaker 6 (Sana): One more security ask: KMS rotation policy and key custody details must be documented for legal.
06:45 Speaker 1 (Miles): Noted — we’ll include rotation cadence, BYOK steps, and HSM notes in the doc.
06:52 Speaker 4 (Leila): Marketing assets — our marketplace requires two hero images (1200x675) and a short demo video (60s). Do you already have these?
06:59 Speaker 1 (Miles): We have logos and an approved 60s explainer; I’ll send the assets link.
07:06 Speaker 2 (Evan): In terms of responsibilities for the joint solution page, who will draft it? Redwood or AuroraCloud?
07:12 Speaker 7 (Amir): We can draft the product-technical part; AuroraCloud should draft the deployment/marketplace boilerplate and legal text. We’ll produce a joint doc and then hand to marketing for final copy.
07:25 Speaker 5 (Benji): Ops question — do you support blue/green upgrades in private installs?
07:31 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes, we recommend blue/green via canary rollout in the orchestration layer; the reference arch includes a sample rollout policy.
07:40 Speaker 6 (Sana): Anything on data residency? Some customers will require EU-only deployment. Will that be an option?
07:46 Speaker 1 (Miles): Yes — we can pin region in the deployment and recommend region-specific endpoints; we’ll call out region constraints in the listing.
08:00 Speaker 2 (Evan): Great. Let’s align on owners and dates. Miles — you said 12/07 for docs?
08:07 Speaker 1 (Miles): Correct. Priya will own smoke test and Terraform snippets. Benji will provide staging credentials by 12/08. Leila will provide marketplace checklist by 12/06.
08:20 Speaker 4 (Leila): Legal will need SOC2 and an indemnity clause — I’ll loop in our legal contact post-call.
08:30 Speaker 1 (Miles): Awesome. Any blockers we missed?
08:35 Speaker 5 (Benji): One small blocker: our staging quota for GPU is limited this week, might need to schedule the smoke test next week.
08:42 Speaker 3 (Priya): That’s fine — we proposed a validation window 12/10 — we can be flexible to match your GPU availability.
08:50 Speaker 2 (Evan): Perfect.
09:00 Speaker 1 (Miles): Recap of next steps — I’ll send the ref-arch draft + asset link, Priya will push terraform + smoke harness, Benji will provision staging creds, Leila will share marketplace checklist and legal contact. Schedule technical validation for 12/10 — I’ll send an invite.
09:20 Speaker 4 (Leila): Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
09:25 Speaker 2 (Evan): Thanks.
09:28 Speaker 3 (Priya): Thanks all, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: Automatic transcription had a few errors around product jargon (KV cache appeared as K V cache and some acronyms were mis-lettered). Speakers sometimes truncated names; action items clarified at end of call.
